component.name: Stellarshot
component.summary: See your backups from the panel

description.p: A COSMIC panel applet for Stellarshot, the backup application. One icon shows whether a backup is running, has failed, has fallen overdue, or found damage. Its popup lists each backup with when it last backed up, what that backup took in, and what has happened since, and its right-click menu backs everything up, restores files, starts a new backup, or opens or quits Stellarshot.
Add it from COSMIC Settings' panel applet list. Closing Stellarshot's window minimizes it to the applet while it is on a panel.

screenshot.caption: Each backup's last backup and what happened since, beside the right-click menu

description.p: A more useful panel applet, and a search that tells versions apart.

ul.li: The applet shows what each backup last did and when, with the last backup's size and changes, and its right-click menu backs everything up, restores, starts a new backup or quits.
A new panel icon, and the applet's popup laid out as a menu.
Search everywhere lists each version of a file with its size and modification time, showing a file that never changed only once, and Show marks the file in its folder, ready to restore.
A backup's page no longer offers a password field while the saved password is still being fetched.

description.p: A password in an address can no longer show through in an error message, and every dependency is up to date.

ul.li: A REST server password holding a slash, question mark, hash or backslash could be shown in part in an error; any address that could be read more than one way is now hidden whole.
libcosmic and the other libraries Stellarshot is built on are updated to their newest versions.

description.p: Safer restores and cleaner credentials, and ready for the COSMIC Store.

ul.li: Closing the restore page no longer stops a running cloud backup, and a snapshot dated in the future no longer makes "Keep for N days" forget the others.
A crafted snapshot can no longer write outside the folder being restored into, and opening someone else's repository no longer takes over their folders.
Sign-in tokens are removed with their backup, downloads are private, and closing the window quits when there is nothing to watch.
Scheduled backups and drives work inside a Flatpak, and the panel applet has a store listing of its own.

description.p: A keyring that is locked is asked to unlock.

ul.li: After logging in without typing the login password, a remembered backup password was not found and a new one could not be saved. The keyring's own unlock prompt now appears when a backup is opened.
